announcements.name: Codex Spark on Cerebras Inference
announcements.shortDescription: A lighter, faster variant of Codex that delivers responses in seconds, positioned as a daily driver for interactive coding.
announcements.longDescription: Codex Spark is described as a lighter, faster version of Codex running on Cerebras Inference. The speed Cerebras provides has made it Jason Liu's daily driver, with tasks running incredibly fast. The speakers note the speed is already there and the intelligence is catching up, and they intend to demo automations users can build themselves in the app.

announcements.name: Multi-agent automation in Codex Spark
announcements.shortDescription: A main agent can interpret a developer's daily goals and dispatch fast Spark sub-agents to read sources like Slack, Google Drive, and Google Meets.
announcements.longDescription: Codex Spark allows defining multi-agents, where a main agent is responsible for understanding the developer's daily goals. That main agent can kick off fast Spark sub-agents to read sources like Slack, Google Drive, and Google Meets, helping the developer understand what's happening within the company and their responsibilities.

announcements.name: Roadmap toward smarter models
announcements.shortDescription: The speakers state the current release is "v1" and that models on Cerebras will grow more intelligent, with future Spark versions absorbing tasks currently limited to full Codex.
announcements.longDescription: Jason Liu emphasizes that the current release is just v1 and that the models on Cerebras are going to get smarter. Sarah Chieng adds that tasks which are Codex-only today might become possible in Spark tomorrow, encouraging developers to learn the tools now ahead of future Spark v2 and v3 releases. Liu contrasts full Codex as a slower, smarter "bus for the mind" with Spark as a fast car that gets you there faster if you know what you're doing.
